chodorowReich.citation: Gabriel Chodorow-Reich, Brookings Papers on Economic Activity (2014)

events.speaker: Ben Bernanke
events.title: The Economic Outlook
events.context: Bernanke told Congress that incoming employment and inflation data could justify changing the pace of asset purchases. In the hearing he raised the possibility of slowing purchases within a few meetings if conditions continued to improve. Two studies measured the Treasury reaction over different windows.

observations.method: The study places the news at 10:30. It compares the yield on the current 5-year note using average indicative bid and ask prices in each interval.
Rosa gives an approximate change and describes the window as one hour around the event. The endpoints are unspecified.

events.speaker: Ben Bernanke
events.title: Federal Reserve Policies in the Financial Crisis
events.context: Speaking in Austin, Bernanke described buying longer-term Treasury or agency securities as one way the Fed could lower borrowing costs as the policy rate approached zero.

observations.method: The study places the speech at 13:45. It compares the yield on the current 5-year note using average indicative bid and ask prices in each interval.

events.speaker: Roger Ferguson Jr.
events.title: Business Continuity after September 11
events.context: Ferguson spoke in Geneva about how banks could keep payments flowing through a disruption. The US Census Bureau also scheduled its factory-orders release for 10 a.m. that day. Both events matter when interpreting the equity move.

observations.method: Rosa measures the price return on the nearest unexpired E-mini S&P 500 contract. This contract tracks US stocks.

events.speaker: Alan Greenspan
events.title: The Economy
events.context: Greenspan told the Bay Area Council that signs of economic stabilization had emerged. He also described risks to the recovery, including weak business investment. Two-year yields fell in the first ten minutes.

observations.method: Rosa measures the yield on the current 2-year Treasury note using indicative dealer quotes at release time and ten minutes later.
